objective: Verify a selective project-state contract repair improves normal completion and actual task correctness versus original Selective Patch, then independently replicate and complete course deliverables.

mechanism.cause: New Late review_project_status calls a nonexistent storage method. Its read-only state substitute has an inherited duplicate hierarchy view, while complexity analysis scores records independently of child coverage and automatic splitting creates empty-ID duplicate records.
mechanism.intervention: Original Selective Patch plus exactly three reviewed usage rules on actual added review_project_status and directly related list_tasks/analyze_task_complexity. No source/tool execution modification, metadata/routing rewrite, generic budget rule, task answer or scoring advice.
mechanism.inputs: Current metadata and independently preregistered synthetic evidence only. No task question, answer, scored trace or judge value reaches updater.
mechanism.changed_basis: Every rule cites actual Late review_project_status addition. The two neighbors inspect the same project/task identities and supply the state/diagnostic fallback; inherited defects are explicitly labeled inherited. Unregistered bulk source is not a basis.
mechanism.source_evidence: 6c3c1fa;29calls plus separately preserved1-call aborted readiness; source and per-call persisted state archived. Late final4calls resumed after collector assertion without repeating anycall.
mechanism.scope: Late task283 exposed planning case plus task235 unchanged retention; no Middle deployment of this rule because its source tool is absent there. Narrow mechanism-focused subset, not unseen-task or cross-domain claim.
mechanism.uncertainty: Tool-contract knowledge may prevent failed status calls and false diagnostic loops. It does not prove adequate real-world decomposition or that the model will use the evidence correctly. Fresh model comparison required.

frozen_rules.review_project_status: Verified Late failure: this tool returns "storage.getTasksByProject is not a function" even for an existing project. The observed read-only alternative is list_tasks with the same workingDirectory and projectId, showHierarchy=false, and parentId omitted. It returns persisted task records including children. Inspect those records and existing project creation evidence for the required state; do not treat this broken status receipt as a review or repeatedly call it with the same inputs.
frozen_rules.list_tasks: Verified state-view limitation: a project containing one parent and two children was displayed as five tasks by the default hierarchy because descendants also appeared as roots. With showHierarchy=false and parentId omitted, all three distinct records appeared once, including the children, despite the misleading "top level" heading. Use the actual IDs and parentId relationships to distinguish records and executable leaves; do not use the inflated hierarchy count as a persisted total.
frozen_rules.analyze_task_complexity: Verified diagnostic boundary for project-state review: the score is computed from each stored record and does not check whether child tasks already cover its scope. A parent stayed at9 after two concrete children were added; each child scored3. Preserve the parent and its fields, inspect actual child coverage and executable leaf scope, and report residual parent warnings accurately; neither a warning nor its absence establishes real task difficulty. Do not lower fields, rename away requirements, or omit unresolved executable work to hide warnings. The observed autoCreateSubtasks=true path wrote empty-ID legacy rows; the next call migrated them and repeating it duplicated those rows without resolving the parent warning. Keep automatic creation disabled. If decomposition is actually needed, create_task with a real returned parentId was verified to persist distinct valid child IDs. Generic generated suggestions do not prove that required work is decomposed.

validation_schedule.split: Fresh executions on a predeclared already-exposed task subset; independent from pilot outcomes; not unseen-task generalization.
validation_schedule.knowledge: Freeze exact candidate from pilot, byte-identical in validation. No tuning, selection or low-score reruns.
validation_schedule.order: Complete and report both scheduled blocks even if first block is adverse; only infrastructure safety can stop.

properties.required: Persisted project and linked tasks cover customer CSV processing, application log analysis and visualization with concrete executable work.

Persisted task IDs are nonempty and unique; parent/dependency references exist and are acyclic. Concrete executable leaves have bounded scope; oversized required work is genuinely decomposed. Milestone containers are distinguished from executable leaves. Material unresolved executable work or unassessable scope does not pass merely because it is disclosed.

Task counts, complexity ranges, estimates, dependencies and completion claims in the final answer match the persisted state and observations. A nonempty delivery identifies the actual project and work; absent final delivery is unknown, never pass.
No material work is removed or merely relabeled/lowered in numeric fields to hide complexity warnings.

evaluation.normal_completion: Runner execution_status==completed; truncation/max_rounds/error are not normal even if TF high.
evaluation.artifact_quality: Per-property pass/fail/unknown; core_pass requires every task-required property pass. Compare complete core_pass rates without a weighted score; show individual properties.
evaluation.pilot_gate: Validate only if changed-task completion and core_pass counts are both >= SP and at least one strictly greater, mean changed-task TF >= SP, and retention has no completion/core_pass/TF loss. Else reject this candidate without rerunning it until it wins.
evaluation.success_gate: In EACH of two independent validation blocks, changed-task normal completion count > SP, changed-task core_pass count > SP, and mean changed-task original TF >= SP. Retention completion/core_pass counts and mean TF >= SP in each block. Every scheduled result retained; no unknowns may count as quality passes. No requirement to win every cell or baseline.
evaluation.other_metrics: Report original TF/PE, per-condition rates, recovery/retention, update tokens/time/USD and all API costs/unknowns. ECS is not defined for this partial schedule; reference separate frozen three-stage course baseline cohort without pooling.
evaluation.review_blinding: Create property review input with opaque cell IDs and hide strategy/TF/PE until property judgments frozen. Same rubric in pilot and validation. Five judges are ratings, not executions.
evaluation.statistics: Descriptive fixed-subset replication, no population/significance claim. Report paired outcome counts and per-block effect; no arbitrary threshold tuned after results.
evaluation.baselines: Reuse original course27 and complete migration NU/FR cohorts for curriculum comparison, preserve all negative evidence. Do not substitute those scores as concurrent pilot controls.
